truths.truth: A user reaches the risk-surface interview deliberately through `/cad-config --surfaces`, and that arm shows the answered set beside what detect-surfaces evidences NOW (ROADMAP criterion 1)
truths.evidence: Wired end to end as prose: skills/cad-config/SKILL.md:4 (argument-hint) and :23 (Routing) -> cadence-core/workflows/config.md:22 (`## 1. Route` branch) -> `## Risk surfaces (--surfaces)` steps 1-5 (config.mjs get -> detect-surfaces --root . --answered -> side-by-side -> ask-user -> set). I ran the arm's two read commands against /code/cadence myself: `config.mjs get review.triggers.risk_surface.surfaces` returns ["secrets","destructive","untrusted_input"], and `detect-surfaces --root . --answered secrets,destructive,untrusted_input` returns inconclusive:true, evidenced:[] and exactly two options - all eight first, then those same three - i.e. the envelope the arm renders is exactly what UAT item 1 expects. What no probe can settle is the RENDERING: whether a live skill run prints them side by side, labels the first `(recommended)` and pre-selects nothing.

truths.truth: Opening the arm and declining leaves .planning/config.json byte-identical (ROADMAP criterion 2)
truths.evidence: Code side holds: the arm's only writer is `config.mjs set` at workflows/config.md step 5, guarded by "Write ONLY on an explicit pick" and "A decline calls no `set` and edits no file"; cmdDetectSurfaces (cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:2821-2930) only readdirs and reads manifests and never writes, and `config.mjs get` is a read. I ran both read steps against this repo with an md5 pinned before and after: `.planning/config.json: OK`, `git status --porcelain` unchanged. The decline PATH through a live skill run is the half no probe reaches.

truths.truth: Every option the interview offers states a reason that describes the set it actually carries - the goal's 'see the evidence for it' half
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/surface-scan.mjs:325-345. With NOTHING answered on an evidencing tree, `held` is empty so `gap === evidenced`, the union candidate (:340) is emitted, and the evidenced-only candidate (:345, reason 'only what the structure evidences') is dropped by the dedup as a repeat. Observed on the #206 demo tree: option 1's set is right (the six) but its reason reads 'the answered set plus what the scan now evidences beyond it: auth (directory auth/), ...' when there is no answered set. That is the FIRST-fire path - the only one most projects ever see, and the exact scenario #206 was filed from. The file's own ORDER comment at :285 states the opposite of what the code does ('with nothing answered, 2 collapses onto 4'; the dedup keeps the EARLIER candidate, so 4 collapses onto 2 and 2's reason is what the user reads), and the guard comment at :336 already rejects this exact failure mode for the mirror case ('a reason ... that names nothing').

truths.truth: The evidence-gap callout - naming every evidenced category the answered set does not cover - is stated AND held in place, on the same 'checked rather than assumed' terms criterion 6 sets for the other rendering clauses
truths.evidence: Stated: cadence-core/workflows/config.md:47 ('call out every evidenced category the answered set does not contain. That gap is the whole reason this arm exists'). Not held: prose-agreement.test.mjs:1853's RULES list pins four ask-user clauses at that same section and this is not among them, so the sentence can be deleted with the whole suite green. Nor does any scenario exercise it - the only tree anyone runs the arm against (/code/cadence) evidences zero categories, which I confirmed (inconclusive:true, evidenced:[]), so the arm passes its human check with the callout absent. This is the plan's own Must-be-true bullet and the SUMMARY's medium open item.

gaps.name: On a first fire the second option's reason names an answered set that does not exist
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - with `held` empty the union candidate (surface-scan.mjs:340) wins the dedup over the evidenced-only candidate (:345), so the option carrying the six evidenced categories is presented as 'the answered set plus what the scan now evidences beyond it' to a project that has answered nothing
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/surface-scan.mjs:325-345. Observed on the freshly built #206 demo tree with no --answered: option 1 = [auth,migrations,billing,concurrency,api_contract,untrusted_input], reason = 'the answered set plus what the scan now evidences beyond it: auth (directory auth/), migrations (directory migrations/), billing (dependency stripe), concurrency (directory workers/), api_contract (directory api/), untrusted_input (dependency express)'. The sets are correct and distinct, so UAT item 3 still passes; what is wrong is the sentence the user reads on the most common path. The file's own ORDER comment at :285 asserts the opposite resolution ('with nothing answered, 2 collapses onto 4'), and the guard comment at :336 already refuses this exact shape for the mirror case.
gaps.missing: Gate the union candidate on `held.length && gap.length` rather than `gap.length` alone, so an unanswered project falls through to the evidenced-only candidate and its 'only what the structure evidences: ...' reason; then correct the :285 comment to say 4 collapses onto 2 when an answer exists. Add a surface-scan.test.mjs row asserting the unanswered evidenced arm's second reason does not mention an answered set.

gaps.reason: unwired - the plan's Must-be-true clause exists only as a sentence in workflows/config.md with no check holding it there and no scenario that would notice its absence
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/workflows/config.md:47 states it. cadence-core/bin/prose-agreement.test.mjs:1853's RULES list pins the four ask-user clauses at that same `## Risk surfaces` section and omits this one, so deleting the sentence leaves the suite green (2476/2477 unchanged). The only tree the human check runs against, /code/cadence, returns inconclusive:true with evidenced:[] (I confirmed via `detect-surfaces --root . --answered secrets,destructive,untrusted_input`), so the callout can never fire there either. Named as a medium open item by the plan review and repeated in SUMMARY.md.
gaps.missing: Add the callout to the RULES list checked at the workflows/config.md site (a claim-shaped regex, e.g. /evidenced categor\w+ the answered set does not contain/i, applied to that site only), so the sentence cannot be dropped silently. To observe it once for real, run the human check a second time inside a copy of the #206 demo tree with `review.triggers.risk_surface.surfaces` answered as ["secrets"] - the arm must then name auth, migrations, billing, concurrency, api_contract and untrusted_input as uncovered.

human_checks.name: In a fresh session, reinstall the plugin from cadence/v3.5.7, /clear, and run `/cad-config --surfaces` in /code/cadence
human_checks.expected: The turn shows the answered set ["secrets","destructive","untrusted_input"] beside the scan's own result (inconclusive: true, evidenced: []) - said plainly as 'the structure evidences nothing either way', not as a clean bill - and then asks with exactly two options: all eight FIRST and labelled (recommended), the current three second, neither pre-selected. Both `config.mjs get review.triggers.risk_surface.surfaces` and `detect-surfaces --root . --answered ...` should appear in the transcript.
human_checks.why_human: Not a truth left unexercised - a resource out of reach: `/cad-config` is a slash command whose body is a skill, and no agent can invoke a skill. I verified everything up to the seam by running the arm's two read commands myself (the envelope they return is exactly what this item expects); what remains is what a MODEL does with that envelope on screen, which only a live session produces.

human_checks.name: Decline that question, then check `git status --porcelain .planning/config.json` and re-read the key
human_checks.expected: git status prints nothing and `node cadence-core/bin/config.mjs config.mjs get review.triggers.risk_surface.surfaces` still returns ["secrets","destructive","untrusted_input"].
human_checks.why_human: Same out-of-reach resource: the decline only exists inside a live `/cad-config --surfaces` run. The code half is already settled - the arm's sole writer is `config.mjs set` on an explicit pick, detect-surfaces never writes, and running both read steps against this repo left config.json's md5 and the working tree unchanged - so what a human is adding is that a real decline takes the no-write path.
